claims.statement: The frontend is a SvelteKit 2 / Svelte 5 SSR application built with Vite and @sveltejs/adapter-node, styled with Tailwind 4 and shadcn-svelte/bits-ui primitives, and charted with lightweight-charts; it exposes two interchangeable import aliases, SvelteKit's $lib/* and the shadcn-style @/*, both mapped to src/lib.

frontend/src/hooks.server.ts guards every request: it verifies the auth_token cookie with jose jwtVerify against JWT_SECRET using HS256, accepts only tokens whose scope is 'access' (deleting the cookie for anything else, including mfa_pending tokens), redirects unauthenticated non-/auth requests 303 to /auth/login, and redirects authenticated users away from /auth/login and /auth/signup to /.

A ?clear_session=true request to /auth/login or /auth/signup deletes any surviving auth_token cookie, sets locals.user to null, and renders the page instead of redirecting, which breaks the redirect loop caused by a stale cookie.

The root load (+layout.server.ts) returns { user: locals.user, sidebar_open, collapsed_watchlist_ids, watchlist_order, watchlist_sort }. When locals.user is set it makes one getUserPreferencesService(fetch).getPreferences(token) call, copies each field across only after a shape check (boolean for sidebar_open, Array.isArray for the two list fields, object for watchlist_sort), and wraps the call in a try/catch that swallows failures so the defaults — sidebar_open true, empty collapsed ids, null order/sort — are returned when the preferences endpoint is unreachable.

Authenticated pages follow a uniform server pattern: the load and each form action construct a client through the factory with SvelteKit's fetch and pass the raw auth_token as an explicit Authorization Bearer override, on ApiError 401 they delete the cookie and redirect 303 to /auth/login?clear_session=true, other statuses are re-thrown as SvelteKit error(status, message), and unknown failures become error(500, 'Internal Server Error').

The /security/[security_id] load fetches the security and its price history in parallel with Promise.all inside getChartDateWindow(..., '1d'), propagates ApiError status codes except 401, and throws a 404 when the price response contains no items; it also re-throws an already-SvelteKit error rather than wrapping it.

Mutations use SvelteKit form actions that validate request.formData() and return fail(status, { message }) on ApiError; the shared EditableTitle component drives inline rename by posting to a named action or calling an onSave callback, using enhance from $app/forms. Login is the exception that writes the auth_token cookie directly (path '/', httpOnly, sameSite lax, secure outside dev, one-week maxAge) across its login, verify2fa, and passkeyLogin actions.

The abstract ApiClient base resolves its origin in one place — browser: VITE_API_BASE_URL or same-origin, server: VITE_INTERNAL_API_URL falling back to VITE_API_BASE_URL — strips a trailing slash, and appends /api/v1, so all client endpoints are relative to the versioned API root.

Every ApiClient request sets credentials: 'include', and an optional tokenOverride adds an Authorization Bearer header used for SSR where a server-to-server fetch does not forward the browser cookie. postFormData omits Content-Type so the multipart boundary is set by the browser, and delete returns undefined for a 204 response instead of parsing a body.

handleResponse throws ApiError for any non-ok response, and extractErrorMessage prefers the JSON detail field (FastAPI's shape), then message, then falls back to 'Request failed with status <status>'; the resulting message string is preserved so components can surface backend text directly.

Each API client module exports a factory getXxxService(customFetch?) alongside a default instance; SSR uses the factory so SvelteKit's load fetch is injected, while the default instance serves browser calls where the cookie is sent automatically.

The API layer covers separate backend areas with distinct clients: AccountClient (accounts, totals, holdings, sync, CSV), AccountService (cross-account holdings), AuthService (login, 2FA verify, passkey auth, signup, verify-email, logout, WS ticket), SecurityClient (/auth/2fa/* and /auth/passkeys/*), BrokerClient (/integration and /external), MarketService (search, prices, securities, watchlists), PortfolioClient, UserPreferencesService, IndicatorsService, AlertsService, NotesService, DocumentsService, SnapshotsService, and AIService.

The route table covers a dashboard at /, account detail at /accounts/[id], broker management at /brokers, security analysis at /security/[security_id], 2FA and passkey management at /settings/security, and the /auth/login, /auth/signup, /auth/logout, and /auth/verify-email auth routes, with /auth/verify-email's load reading the token query parameter and returning a success/error status.

Complex state and orchestration live in ES6 classes in *.svelte.ts files using runes ($state, $derived, $derived.by) rather than in .svelte components or legacy svelte/store: AccountsListState owns accounts, selection mode, groupBy, a SvelteSet of syncing account ids, and a record of per-account sync error messages, seeding from the SSR-provided accounts.
ModalState<T> in lib/utils/modal-state.svelte.ts is a reusable rune class exposing isOpen, data, open(), close(), and reset(), shared by every create/view/delete modal in the app.

+layout.svelte instantiates layout-scoped services at component init via setBrokerService(), setSecurityService(), and setWatchlistService(), which publish them with setContext under symbol keys; consumers call the matching getXxxService(), which returns the context instance, or a fresh instance when given a customFetch for SSR, or — for SecurityService only — a lazily created module-level defaultService when called outside a component hierarchy.

The state layer enforces hard rules: never destructure reactive primitives (it severs the Svelte 5 proxy and breaks reactivity), use $effect for side effects such as DOM listeners and load triggers rather than for computing state or fetching data, and declare a property with $state if the whole reference will be reassigned since deep-proxied objects allow in-place mutation without redeclaration.

No module-level instantiated state class or raw exported $state may be exported from a .svelte.ts file, because in an SSR environment that bleeds one user's state into another user's request; the instance must be created in a component or layout and passed down through context.

Multi-step fetches are orchestrated inside a single service method rather than sequenced in a component: AccountsListState.syncAccount posts the sync request and then polls getSyncStatus until the account leaves the in-flight list, and WatchlistService.addSecurity resolves-or-creates the security with createOrUpdateSecurity, short-circuits when the target list already contains that security id (the backend does not dedupe membership), and only then posts the membership request.

Services store real error message strings rather than a generic boolean error flag — BrokerService, WatchlistService, and SecurityService each expose an error string, and AccountsListState keeps a per-account syncErrors record — so the UI layer can render actionable feedback; all API calls in frontend tests must be mocked, since CI runs without a backend and an unmocked fetch fails the suite.

AccountsListState opens a WebSocket to /api/ws (URL derived from an absolute VITE_API_BASE_URL when present, otherwise from window.location) using a short-lived signed ticket from authService.getWsTicket(), maintains syncingAccountIds and syncErrors from the sync_started, sync_finished, and sync_failed event types, hydrates in-flight syncs from the sync-status endpoint on open, and reconnects on a 5-second timer after close.

syncAccount guards against lost pub/sub messages by polling the sync-status endpoint in waitForSyncFinish with a 60-second deadline, a 1.5-second interval, and a 5-second grace period after the account leaves the in-flight list, clearing the sync state and refetching accounts or setting a timeout error message.

The authenticated shell in +layout.svelte composes Sidebar.Provider bound to a sidebarOpen state seeded from data.sidebar_open inside untrack, with AppSidebar and Sidebar.Inset wrapping page content; it instantiates the layout-scoped services, runs a single $effect that calls watchlistService.loadWatchlists() once data.user is set, persists sidebar changes through userPreferencesService.patchPreferences({ sidebar_open: open }), owns globalSearchOpen plus globalSearchTargetWatchlist, publishes them via setContext('toggleGlobalSearch') and setContext('openGlobalSearch'), and renders GlobalSearch with bind:open and bind:targetWatchlist.

AppSidebar is collapsible to icon size and stacks AppSidebarHeader (brand link to / plus the sidebar trigger), AppSidebarActions (a Search entry invoking the toggleGlobalSearch context callback with a Cmd-P hint, and a Watchlists link to /watchlists), AppSidebarWatchlist (renders every watchlist from getWatchlistService().watchlists as a collapsible group, not just the default one), and AppSidebarProfile (footer dropdown with the user email and navigation to /brokers, /settings/security, and a native POST form to /auth/logout).

GlobalSearch is a Command.Dialog bound to the layout's open state and to a $bindable targetWatchlist; it debounces marketService.search by 300 ms, groups results by security_type, and on select calls createOrUpdateSecurity then goto('/security/{id}'). Its star button is target-aware: it resolves the bound target against the service's current watchlists, matches a result by symbol plus exchange, and either removes/adds membership on that target list or — with no target — falls back to defaultWatchlistSecurities and delegates to toggleSecurity, so an existing security is toggled rather than re-created. Closing the dialog resets the query, the results, and the bound target, and Cmd/Ctrl+P is bound at the document level in +layout.svelte.

Type and money conventions: backend fields are mirrored as snake_case, list endpoints return PaginatedResponse<T> with an items array, and Money is { value?, units?, nanos?, currencyCode? } where moneyToNumber prefers units plus nanos/1e9 and falls back to parsing the string value while money() renders a localized dollar amount. Account holdings totals are nested as { cost: Money, value: Money }.

Account and institution domain enums live in lib/types/account.ts with getAccountTypeLabel and getInstitutionLabel helpers that accept an optional translate callback, and AccountHoldings extends PaginatedResponse<Holding> with account-level totals (total_value, total_profit_loss, total_profit_loss_percent, net_deposits, currency) consumed by the account detail header and HoldingsTable.

Frontend tests use Vitest with jsdom and @testing-library/svelte configured in vite.config.ts (environment jsdom, url http://localhost/, setupFiles ./src/setupTest.ts, include src/**/*.test|spec), with setupTest.ts registering jest-dom, stubbing window.location, and deferring teardown ~50 ms so bits-ui body-scroll-lock timers do not throw after jsdom is destroyed; tests must mock every API client module and stub each method the component calls, and must also mock framework or third-party modules that reach the network or DOM ($app/forms, $app/paths, $app/navigation, $app/stores, lightweight-charts), replacing global.WebSocket in websocket tests.

hooks.server.test.ts runs under the node vitest environment, mocks $env/static/private, signs real HS256 tokens with jose for each case, and covers token-scope rejection such as mfa_pending tokens clearing the cookie while leaving locals.user null.

The frontend extension points are consistent: a new backend area is a class extending ApiClient exported as both a getXClient factory and a default instance; a new page is a +page.server.ts with the standard 401-delete-and-redirect / ApiError-to-error shape over a thin +page.svelte shell; a new stateful feature is a Foo.svelte.ts rune class with isLoading and message-valued error state instantiated in a component or provided from +layout.svelte; and a new preference is a field added to UserPreferences in userPreferencesService.ts, patched from the component with patchPreferences, and — when it drives layout rendering — also read in +layout.server.ts's load behind a shape check inside the existing try/catch.

The /watchlists route's server load reads the auth_token cookie, calls getMarketService(fetch).getWatchlists(token), and returns { watchlists }; on ApiError it deletes the cookie and redirects 303 to /auth/login?clear_session=true for a 401, re-throws error(status, message) for other statuses, and throws error(500, 'Internal Server Error') for unexpected failures.

The /watchlists page renders one section per watchlist with security links to /security/{id}, formatted price and daily-change pills, inline rename, a confirmation-modal delete, per-watchlist sort selection, and a Reorder mode with drag-and-drop. It reads the shared WatchlistService instance from context (seeding watchlistService.watchlists from its SSR data only when the service is still empty), keeps its own watchlistOrder/watchlistSort $state seeded from data or $page.data, and persists reorders and sort choices as fire-and-forget patchPreferences({ watchlist_order }) / patchPreferences({ watchlist_sort }) calls. Its per-watchlist '+' button calls the layout's openGlobalSearch context callback with that watchlist.

WatchlistService is the single client-side owner of watchlist data: its constructor only wires getMarketService(customFetch), loadWatchlists(token) stores the array returned by GET /market/watchlists directly (each watchlist already carries its embedded securities, so there is no resolve-then-fetch step), defaultWatchlistSecurities is a $derived lookup for name === 'Default' that backs hasSecurity and toggleSecurity (and therefore the id-less addToWatchlist/removeFromWatchlist shortcuts), and every write returning a WatchlistRead goes through replaceWatchlist(updated) which swaps one element by id while createWatchlist appends and deleteWatchlist filters. removeSecurityFromWatchlist and toggleSecurity re-run loadWatchlists in their catch to resynchronise after a failed write, whereas removeSecurity only records the error message.

Layout-level preferences are server-loaded and client-persisted in one round trip: sidebar_open, collapsed_watchlist_ids, watchlist_order and watchlist_sort are all read in +layout.server.ts and written back with userPreferencesService.patchPreferences from the component owning the interaction (the layout's sidebar handler, AppSidebarWatchlist.toggleCollapsed, and the /watchlists drop and sort handlers), always as fire-and-forget calls that only log on failure. sidebar_watchlists is declared on UserPreferences but is not read by any component or load.

Watchlist ordering and collapse state are presentation layers over the shared service data: sortWatchlistsByOrder(watchlists, order) in watchlist-utils.ts sorts by index in the persisted id array and appends watchlists absent from it in their original relative order, and sortSecurities(securities, sortKey) implements the name_asc, name_desc, price_change_desc and price_change_asc keys. AppSidebarWatchlist resolves watchlist_order and collapsed_watchlist_ids from a setContext seam first (used by app-sidebar.test-harness.svelte), then from $page.data, keeps collapse state in a SvelteSet, and persists the whole set on toggle; the /watchlists page applies the same two helpers to the same service data.

MarketService covers both watchlist membership styles plus the paginated per-list read: the id-less default-list shortcuts POST/DELETE /market/watchlists/securities/{securityId} (backed by addToWatchlist/removeFromWatchlist), the per-list POST/DELETE /market/watchlists/{watchlistId}/securities/{securityId} (addSecurityToWatchlist/removeSecurityFromWatchlist), and GET /market/watchlists/{watchlistId}/securities returning PaginatedResponse of SecuritySchema, alongside watchlist list/create/rename/delete.

setupTest.ts additionally no-ops Element.prototype.scrollIntoView because bits-ui's Command calls it asynchronously on the active item and closest group heading, and suppresses only the DEV-only derived_inert console warning emitted by bits-ui's dismissible-layer afterSleep timers while forwarding every other warning.

Route-level tests exercise the shell and page components directly with mocked clients instead of a running server: routes/layout.test.ts renders +layout.svelte with a createRawSnippet child to assert the unauthenticated bare-children path versus the Sidebar.Provider path and calls the +layout.server.ts load with a fake event to check collapsed_watchlist_ids, watchlist_order and watchlist_sort defaults, and routes/watchlists/page.svelte.test.ts mocks the market client and preferences service while keeping a real WatchlistService instance (mocking only getWatchlistService) so the page's $derived ordering and sorting run against real rune state.
